name: table-count
description: Number of Drizzle pgTable() definitions across shared/. The mature-machine north star is a SMALLER schema (<=450 tables); today's count is far above it. This strict down-only ratchet makes the schema monotonic: adding a table fails CI until the baseline is deliberately bumped (a conscious 'yes we need this'), and every consolidation lowers the baseline toward the target. Founder-chosen 'strict' 2026-07-16.
lastBumpNote: 758 -> 759 on 2026-08-12: outward_actions -- idempotency at the ACTION/PROVIDER boundary (canonical law 8, BI74). Earned by a concrete money-losing defect, not a feature. server/middleware/idempotency.ts is HTTP-REQUEST-scoped (Idempotency-Key header, 24h TTL, in-memory fallback) and protects a client retrying a POST; it does NOTHING for the case that actually costs money -- a background JOB retrying after a partial success, which never passes through an HTTP request at all. directMailService.sendLetter() deducts credits, posts the Lob piece cost to the ledger, then calls Lob; if the process dies after Lob accepted the letter but before the result was recorded, the retry deducts credits AGAIN, posts cost AGAIN, and prints a SECOND physical letter to a real seller. preMailDedupe.ts does not catch it -- that is an AUDIENCE policy (don't mail your own parcel, don't re-mail within 90 days), not retry safety. The UNIQUE (organization_id, action_kind, idempotency_key) index IS the mechanism: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means exactly one caller wins, so two concurrent workers cannot both call the provider. Unlike evidence_claims and decision_snapshots this table is deliberately MUTABLE -- it is OPERATIONAL STATE (claimed -> succeeded/failed/ambiguous), not history; BI76 is explicit that audit events, decision snapshots, action receipts and outcomes are different things that must not collapse into one log, and the immutable proof of an action remains a receipt (autopilot/proofReceipt.ts), a separate artifact with a separate lifecycle. The 'ambiguous' status is the whole point (AU28): a provider timeout AFTER the request left is neither success nor failure, most implementations treat it as failure and retry, and that is exactly how a double-send happens -- here it is terminal and REFUSES further attempts until reconciliation, so the system stops and asks rather than guessing with someone else's money.
